methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $15M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.5x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
fab2 is a seed-stage chip design company founded by Jim Keller and Sam Zeloof, operating in a competitive sector populated by 3 public comps (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched. The company has raised $15M+ to date.

Stage-progression analysis provides the primary valuation anchor. Using the $15M total raised as a proxy for seed-stage value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields $38M. This method is applicable given the company's clear stage positioning, though it relies on raised capital as a proxy rather than post-money valuation. Peer-median analysis is not feasible: while 12 same-sector peers exist, insufficient overlap exists on stage and valuation tier to support a statistically reliable median (minimum of 3 required). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (median 21.5x across Semiconductors) cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue figures, which private companies rarely provide.

The triangulation range is $32M–$43M, with a median of $38M. This range reflects modest variance bounds (±15%) around the single applicable method rather than true method diversity. Key uncertainties include the actual post-money valuation at fab2's most recent funding round, which would refine the base; competitive positioning relative to the named peer set; and technology differentiation vis-à-vis both established public chipmakers and well-funded private competitors. Additional disclosure of revenue run rate or near-term commercialization milestones would enable public-comp validation.
